$schema_note: Slice 2.1 authoring surface. See _authoring_brief below before editing.
_authoring_brief: WHAT THIS IS. One frame per pose on the MetaHuman face board, expressed as raw
RigLogic control weights rather than as a linear sum of already-baked ARKit shapes.
That difference IS item F2: RigLogic evaluates these controls with its correctives and
co-articulation intact, and reaches the tongue, which the ARKit mapping never exposes.
WHY A TABLE AND NOT A HAND-POSED ASSET. The plan says 'posed on the face board'. Posing
in the GUI and saving the result gives an asset nobody can diff, review, or re-derive for
the next identity. These weights drive the SAME controls the board writes -- CTRL_expressions.*
are the rig's 263 raw controls, confirmed against the DNA -- so this is the board, in a form
that survives review. The operator's job becomes refining numbers while watching, not
rebuilding sixteen poses from scratch.
AND THE HONEST CAVEAT. These starting values were authored from articulatory phonetics
and from the three facts the VISEME_RECIPES comment records, NOT from an on-screen session.
A hand-authored pose encodes its author's assumptions exactly the way a hand-tuned constant
does. Slice 2.1's [V] screenshot review is what turns them from plausible into judged, and
it is not optional: it is the ground truth every later slice compares against.
THE THREE FACTS THE OLD RECIPE COMMENT ENCODES, WHICH STILL HOLD:
1. At rest the lips are CLOSED and no teeth show. viseme_sil is zero-delta, not a pose.
2. mouthFunnel FLARES and parts the lip opening rather than protruding it -- used heavily
it exposes teeth. Rounding comes from PURSE, not funnel. (Here: mouthLipsPurse*.)
3. jawOpen reveals teeth by about 0.05. Closed-mouth consonants keep it at or near zero.
CONVENTIONS. Weights are 0..1 on the named control. Absent control == 0. Names are the
raw control minus the 'CTRL_expressions.' prefix; the exporter lowercases them to the
'ctrl_expressions_<lowername>' curve the AnimSequence carries. Quadrant suffixes are
U/D (upper/lower lip) x L/R (side): mouthLipsPurseUL = upper lip, left.

poses.name: viseme_sil
poses.note: Deliberately zero-delta. Rest already reads as a closed mouth; posing 'neutral' on top of neutral only introduces drift.

poses.name: viseme_PP
poses.note: Bilabial stop. The seal is the whole signature -- lips together and compressed, jaw shut. MEASURED CORRECTION 2026-08-22: at press 0.34 this baked to 4.03 mm against the composed shape's 8.76 mm, i.e. a WEAKER /p/ than the approximation it replaces. Same cause as mouthClose: mouthLipsTogether contributes almost nothing from a closed rest, so press and the roll-in are carrying the pose and had to come up. Compression is the visible part of a bilabial stop -- the lips are already touching before it starts.

poses.name: viseme_FF
poses.note: Labiodental. Lower lip to the UPPER TEETH -- mouthLowerLipTowardsTeeth* is the literal control and the composed recipe had no access to it, approximating with mouthRollLower. Slight upper-lip raise clears the teeth.

poses.name: viseme_TH
poses.note: Interdental -- the tongue tip is VISIBLE between the teeth. This is the pose the composed shape could not make: it had jawOpen + tongueOut and no tip control at all. tongueThin+tongueWide flatten the blade so it reads as a tongue, not a lump.

poses.name: viseme_DD
poses.note: Alveolar stop. Tongue TIP to the ridge behind the upper teeth, jaw barely open so the contact is visible. tonguePress is the contact itself. The composed shape used jawOpen+mouthShrugUpper -- lip cues that merely correlate.

poses.name: viseme_kk
poses.note: Velar. The constriction is at the BACK -- tongue body humped up and retracted, tip DOWN and out of the way. Almost no lip signature, which is why the composed version had nothing to work with.

poses.name: viseme_CH
poses.note: Postalveolar. Lips protruded and rounded, tongue blade raised toward the ridge. Rounding via PURSE per fact 2; a little funnel for the flare, kept low so teeth stay covered.

poses.name: viseme_SS
poses.note: Sibilant. Teeth nearly together, lips spread, tongue grooved just behind the ridge. jawOpen stays at fact 3's teeth-reveal threshold on purpose -- /s/ shows a sliver of teeth and that reads correct.

poses.name: viseme_nn
poses.note: Nasal / lateral. Tongue held ON the ridge -- a sustained version of DD's contact with a smaller aperture. tonguePress higher than DD because the contact is held, not released.

poses.name: viseme_RR
poses.note: Rhotic. Slight rounding plus a BUNCHED tongue -- body raised and retracted, tip loose. The bunch is what makes /r/ read as /r/ rather than as a weak /w/.

poses.name: viseme_aa
poses.note: Open vowel. Jaw is the whole pose. Tongue low and flat so the mouth reads open rather than merely slack. Kept at 0.64 not 1.0 -- jawOpen 1.0 on this rig is 32.7mm, a yawn.

poses.name: viseme_E
poses.note: Mid-front vowel. Moderate opening with the corners drawn slightly wide, tongue mid-high and forward.

poses.name: viseme_I
poses.note: Close-front vowel. Nearly closed and strongly spread -- the widest corners of any pose. Tongue high and narrow.

poses.name: viseme_O
poses.note: Mid-back rounded. Open AND round, which is the combination the old recipe got wrong by leaning on funnel: funnel opened the aperture instead of rounding it. Purse dominant, funnel supporting, tongue retracted.

poses.name: viseme_U
poses.note: Close-back rounded -- the tightest rounding in the set. Purse near maximum, corners drawn in hard, funnel deliberately low (fact 2) and jaw nearly shut.

poses.name: mouthClose
poses.note: ARKit mouthClose seals the LIPS INDEPENDENTLY OF THE JAW. MEASURED CORRECTION 2026-08-22: authored first as mouthLipsTogether* alone, it baked to 0.00 mm -- a dead morph. mouthLipsTogether is a no-op at a CLOSED jaw, because it closes the lips against an OPEN one and there is nothing for it to do from rest; a baked morph can only carry a delta from rest, so that pose encoded nothing. The press/roll terms are what give it real deformation from a closed rest, which is also why the old MOUTHCLOSE_RECIPE reached for them. mouthLipsTogether stays, at weight, so the shape still behaves correctly when lipsync fires it against jawOpen.
